title: Consolidated prefetch service + query shaper to cut tenant-scoped pagination tail latency
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Background: Several dashboard endpoints serving tenant-scoped paginated queries are exhibiting long tail latency during concurrent exploration workflows (large time ranges + high concurrent tenants). Root causes identified in initial incident review: high read amplification from wide-range scans, repeated KV cache misses for common prefixes, and an expensive fanout when cursors traverse many small segments.

Proposal: Implement a consolidated "prefetch" microservice (tenant-aware, multi-tenant cache and async prefetch coordinator) paired with a query-shaper layer in the dashboard API. The prefetch service will warm segment-level micro-rollups and KV prefixes asynchronously, expose a small RPC for the API to request prioritized ranges, and provide telemetry for access patterns. The query shaper rewrites pagination requests to include segment-hints and an adaptive overscan window based on recent access signals (hot page, scan next-n). Together these reduce DB read amplification, improve cache hit rate, and shrink tail latency for paginated dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for paginated dashboard queries reduced by >= 35% on staging for representative tenant load
Average DB read amplification (tokens read per returned row) reduced by >= 40% for targeted endpoints
Integration tests covering cursor semantics (forward/backwards/expiry) pass and match existing API behavior
New prefetch service emits tenant-scoped metrics: prefetch_requests, cache_hit_rate, evictions, avg_fetch_time
Can toggle prefetch behavior via runtime flag per-tenant without schema changes
No customer-facing regressions in A/B rollout on 10% of production traffic (canary)
technical_notes: Architecture: dashboard API -> query-shaper (inline lib) -> prefetch-service (gRPC) -> storage/rollup layer
Prefetch store: in-memory LRU + small SSD-backed segment store for large windows. Key namespace: tenant_id|time_bucket|segment_id
Eviction policy: tenant-weighted LRU with time-bucket TTL. Hot tenants get proportional cache slice to avoid noisy neighbor eviction
Async prefetch: schedule background fetch into prefetch store with read-ahead heuristic derived from per-tenant access slope (exponential smoothing)
Query shaper: when prefetch hints available, rewrite storage read into segment-scoped range requests and bypass wide scans; fall back to original path on miss
Hedging: issue light-weight hedged read for first page when prefetch confidence < threshold to reduce tail without extra load on steady state
Compatibility: cursor format preserved. Preemptively add a cursor version byte to support future migrations but accept current cursors unchanged
Observability: add Tagging to traces with prefetch_id, candidate_segments, prefetch_hit boolean. Create dashboard in Grafana: /dashboards/prefetch/tenant-shape
Datastore considerations: leverage existing materialized micro-rollups (ENG-557321) instead of ad-hoc wide scans; avoid changing primary storage indexes in this change
Failure modes: prefetch-service fallback path goes to existing path; implement circuit-breaker and exponential backoff to avoid cascading failures
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests (0-1 week): implement prefetch client & query-shaper hooks
2) Staging deploy (1 week): deploy prefetch service w/ small memory config, run synthetic load harness against staging traffic patterns
3) Perf tuning (1 week): iterate cache sizing, overscan heuristics, hedging thresholds based on staging metrics
4) Canary (10% production): enable for low-traffic tenants first, monitor prefetch_hit_rate, p95 latency, db read amplification
5) Ramp (weeks): 10% -> 50% -> 100% with performance gates at each step and automatic rollback on error budgets
6) Post-rollout cleanup: remove old debug flags and add dashboard runbook entries
